contradictions: 888poker.com is not listed on Spain's DGOJ operator register; the DGOJ licence covering the '888' brand in Spain is held by a distinct group entity (888 Online Games España, S.A.) and expressly names 888poker.es, not 888poker.com, as the authorised domain.

The entity actually contracting with a given 888poker.com visitor could not be confirmed directly (homepage/terms fetch returned HTTP 403); attribution to 888 UK Limited vs. Virtual Global Digital Services Limited is inferred from the UKGC domain register and a sister-brand licensing page rather than the target site's own disclosure.

The 888/Evoke group is simultaneously a DGOJ-licensed operator in Spain (via its .es entity) and, on the evidence gathered, has no Spanish authorisation for the .com domain under investigation — an unusual profile compared to a typical wholly-unlicensed offshore operator.

priority.rationale: The target domain belongs to a large, LSE-listed, multiply-regulated international group (Evoke plc) that already operates a DGOJ-licensed Spanish sister brand (888poker.es via 888 Online Games España, S.A.). The likely underlying issue is domain-perimeter/geoblocking hygiene at a known, reachable, compliance-engaged operator rather than a covert or evasive black-market gambling scheme. Enforcement value is better captured through a compliance/geoblocking query to the identified corporate group (or referral to UK/Gibraltar/Malta regulators) than through a full illegal-operator case file.

factors.harmAndExposure: No direct evidence of Spanish-language/currency/payment-method targeting on 888poker.com was obtained (direct fetch blocked); the group's standard practice for other regulated markets is to geoblock/redirect to a local licensed domain, which would limit incremental exposure if applied correctly to Spain.
factors.consumerHarmSeverity: Operator is a large, publicly listed, long-established brand with standard player-protection infrastructure on its licensed sites; no Spain-specific fraud or non-payment complaint pattern found. Some genuine control weaknesses exist group-wide (Gibraltar KYC/EDD settlement; DGOJ AML/technical-system fines on the Spanish entity), indicating imperfect but not absent compliance.
factors.legalReachability: Very high — a named, LSE-listed corporate group headquartered in Gibraltar, with an identifiable UK-licensed entity (888 UK Limited, UKGC account 39028) and an existing licensed Spanish subsidiary already in regulatory dialogue with DGOJ.
factors.actorBehaviorIntent: No evidence found of mirror-domain rotation, WHOIS concealment, or evasion tactics for this brand (WHOIS is transparent, registrant is a known group Gibraltar entity); regulatory history shows the group settling/paying fines rather than ignoring warnings.
factors.feasibilityCost: Low — resolution most plausibly requires a compliance/geoblocking verification request to a known, responsive corporate group rather than a resource-intensive covert investigation or asset-tracing exercise.
factors.strategicValue: Limited deterrent value against genuine illegal/black-market gambling, since this is a licensed international operator with a compliant local mirror; pursuing it as a headline illegal-operator case risks conflating a domain-segregation compliance question with true unlicensed operation, diluting campaign credibility.

analystNotes: Direct fetches of https://www.888poker.com/ and its about-us page returned HTTP 403, so brand/entity/licence claims for the target domain itself rely on: (1) the UK Gambling Commission's public domain-names register for account 39028, which independently confirms 888poker.com as an active licensed domain of 888 UK Limited; (2) a sister-brand (888sport.com) licensing page disclosing the group's Gibraltar and Malta entities/licence numbers, used as a proxy for the same corporate group's disclosure pattern; and (3) WHOIS aggregator search snippets showing registrant 'Cassava Enterprises (Gibraltar) Limited' at the same Gibraltar address used by the group's other entities. The single most important structural fact for this case is that Spain's DGOJ has licensed a *different* named entity (888 Online Games España, S.A.) for a *different* domain (888poker.es), and no Spanish authorisation for 888poker.com itself was found. Recommended next steps if this case proceeds: (a) attempt a Spain-geolocated fetch or use a compliance testing tool to confirm whether 888poker.com actually redirects/blocks Spanish IPs to 888poker.es (this could not be tested from this session); (b) obtain 888poker.com's own terms/footer via an alternate access method to name the exact contracting entity; (c) check the Gibraltar Gambling Commissioner's and MGA's own public registers directly (not just secondary sources) to verify RGL 112/113 and MGA/CRP/543/2018 status.
